      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted  in  almost
any form for publication in our
OUTLETTERS: BASIC PRINT or  DATA
statements, handwritten or typed
pages, a simple  JOTTER  program
is provided in Issue 2(Opus #4);
mailbox messages via Prestel No.
014703943 but the easiest for us
to edit are Tasword 2 files with
the right-hand margin set at 32.

Please state if there should  be
parts of your letter you do  not
wish published but we always use
our discretion  anyway.  Letters
may also be edited  for  clarity
and length... Please ask if  you
welcome  direct   correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Gordon Roberts, Cumbria

Hello and thank you for a very
enjoyable magazine. Hello to my
fellow readers too. John Luby
must take the blame for the two
programs that are also on the
cartridge because he did say
"Get your fingers out!" and I
have done just that.

I am a 50 yr old amateur (VERY!)
[dare I say programmer?] "messer
about" on my keyboard. Set-up is
+2, m/d's, Ibico LTR1 printer
(Kem E i/f). I can mess about
for hours on end and achieve
absolutely nothing at all with
the greatest of ease, but I do
enjoy myself. My wife says she
is a computer widow!

This is the first time I've ever
written to any computer magazine
at least I think it is - the old
memory has never been much good,
and I would just like to say
that it is the friendly aura of
OUTLET which has helped give me
the courage to do so. AUTOCHARS?
- Terrific! It's all terrific!
           Bye for now.
               Gordon Roberts.

P.S. If this makes the December
issue then "Compliments of the
season to all". If, as I suspect
it might well be, it is too late
and makes a later one then
"Belated c.o.t.s.t.a."

Thanks, Gordon and w.t.h.d.t.m.
to you! - Brian

From: K.A. Schimmel, Nottingham

Gentlemen,

Could you give me some advice on
CHARCOL and SKETCH as my printer
HR5 gives an automatic linefeed.

I am a keen follower of OUTCLASS
machine code lessons. The first
instruction with an assembler
and not just a hex-loader as in
the 5 books on m/c on my book-
shelf. All 5 books left me more
puzzled than I was before work-
ing through them. Now, thanks to
OUTLET I have actually started
doing something myself instead
of just copying hex numbers and
begin to understand some of the
waffle in the books. Please keep

it as simple as you are doing
now so that we old fogies can
keep up. When you get over the
60 mark (64) the old grey matter
seems to slow down a bit.

With best wishes for all of you
at OUTLET!

           K. Schimmel

To: K. Schimmel from Brian

Research shows that keeping the
mind active regenerates brain
pathways so reducing the slowing
down process  (OUTCLASS reaches
the parts other m/code lessons
can't!).

Study your HR5 manual to find if
the line feed and spacing can be
changed.If so look at lines 5050
to about 6500 in CHARCOL. It is
well commented. You might try
removing the CHR$10 in 5300,5400
and 5600. You might also adjust
the dip switches in the HR5 (see
manual).SKETCH has a m/code high
res dump.It would not be easy to
re-write. Can anyone else advise
on the HR5?         - Brian

From Dr E.J.Wilson

Dear Ron and Brian

At last after receiving a dozen
or so OUTLETs I have plucked up
sufficient courage to drop a
line and really show my ignor-
ance and to say how much I have
enjoyed your efforts during the
past year. I am using JOTTER but
would rather use Tasword 3. Do
you accept such?

I may have a PhD, but as far as
computers are concerned I am one
of those 'thickies' mentioned in
letters recently!

I have a Spectrum +2 with micro-
drives and a Brother M1109

printer. A couple of years ago I
purchased a Swift disc and with
their Emulator have managed to
transfer a lot of my accumulated
word processing data in Tasword
3 onto disc. I am grateful to
Sixword for the patience they
have had with me.

Recently I wanted to print out
the pages dealing with machine
code, but failed to achieve
anything but gibberish following
the usual baud rate entry of
1200 and I for Interface 1. It
wasn't until I bought the early
editions of OUTLET that I real-
ised it was possible to print
the pages without difficulty.
Since then I tested each of the
issues of OUTLET and find that

since you went over to using 2
cartridges the printing does not
materialise.

Not having read any complaint
from anyone else I had assumed
it was my set-up, however since
the first 4 cartridges work OK,
please, please what is wrong.
What am I doing wrong?

Furthermore, one last request
-- can you supply OUTLET on
SWIFTDISCs (MF/2DD)?

Keep up the good work. Maybe I
will write again!!

               TED

To: Ted Wilson from Brian

You've unearthed a bug which has
been in OUTLET all year - it
affects each issue from 5 to 16!
It amazes me that it hasn't been
uncovered before but I can only
put it down to the fact that I
use baud rate 9600 which is the
default baud rate.To correct the
problem BREAK into CONTENTS and
enter GO SUB 9994 (this ensures
that AUTOCHARS not CHUNKY CHARS
is operative - the latter makes
text undreadable when editing).
Move line 1290 to 1291 by using
LIST 1290, EDIT, alter 1290 to
1291 and ENTER. Then enter 1290
to delete line 1290.Use RUN 9980
to re-SAVE. Brian Gaff sent me a
mailbox the other week with what

must have been the same problem!
I didn't twig it at the time.
Sorry Brian!

Yes, use Tasword 3 by all means
but please set the right-hand
margin at 32. It also helps if
you indicate what kind of file
if possible, e.g. scribble Tas 3
file somewhere! (Each month Ron
and I play at "Guess what kind
of file THIS one is!"

Sorry - we can't supply OUTLET
on SWIFTDISK at present. I wish
we could!
                        - Brian

From Percy Ellis, STROUD

I have a full-size printer:
SHINWA CP 80 TYPE 1

I use Tasman Interface software.

I have a Spectrum 48K computer.

I am unable to print any of the
information you give direct- I'm
loathe to spend money on a new
interface - as a pensioner - but
it is driving me round the bend.

Any suggestions? Would it pay me
to get a new interface? If so, a
suitable one and cost please.

Thanks for all the good news.

To: Percy Ellis from Brian

You need a little bit of BASIC
programming knowledge plus read
your Tasman interface manual. If
you read my reply to Ken Hunter
in last month's OUTLETTERs you
will see which lines need to be
altered. You have the extra
problem of loading the code. You
could just load it with a direct
command then run the program
again and print-out. Alternately
you could put it in a REM using
REMSTORE from issue 6. However,
you do not give the address of
the code or its length. I think
it may be around 64000 which
would clash with AUTOCHARS which
is in most programs. You can get
round that by entering:-

9994 RETURN
             ... or altering the
64000 in line 9994 to another
address.

Many programs vary and there are
all sorts of complications so,
unless you are familiar with
programming (and I don't think
you would be asking if you were)
I can only suggest you get an
interface supported by OUTLET.
You appreciate we can only supp-
ort the common interfaces and
Epson-compatible printers or the
entire issue would be full of
printer routines!

It's a pity your printer is not
RS232 as then you could use your
Interface 1. As it is I would

recommend you get the Kempston E
at `37.95 from MICROSNIPS, 37
Seaview Road,Wallasey,Merseyside
L45 4QN. Expensive but you might
check classified ads to pick up
one second-hand.

Sorry,but there's no easy answer
I'm afraid!
                     - Brian

From Andrew Clapham, Nottingham

Dear Brian & Ron,

I still don't know how to alter
the graphics control characters
in Tasword 2 [This is for use
with the Brother M1009 printer]

               Andrew Clapham

I looked at one or two and they
don't NEED altering as the M1009
is fairly epson-compatible. If
you WANT to alter them then use
'g' at the main menu, enter the
CODE number for the graphic (NOT
the graphic itself) then each
code followed by ENTER, finally
ending on just ENTER.To put the
graphics in the text you just
use SHIFT 9.       - Brian

From: Chris Clayton, CARLISLE



Dear Ron/Brian,

Like John Luby I bought the ECHO
keyboard from Omnidale (to give
to my children at Christmas) and
was pleased with it. I would
welcome his advice on how to
transfer the software to micro-
drive and any advice on its use.
In particular I was surprised I
could not output the sound
through my cassette recorder(why
is this?) and as there is a lot
of unwelcome buzz from my TV
speaker I would like to get a
suitable amplifier/leads, but
have no idea what to look for.

ECHO did produce an amplifier to
go with the keyboard (which was
originally for the BBC I under-
stand). Does anyone know if this
is still available?

Something else I need help with
is THE ARTIST II 128. So far a
detailed letter and two phone
calls have not produced any re-
sponse from SOFTECHNICS. I need
help with -

1. How to transfer the programme
to microdrive.

2. How to print via Interface I.
I can get something by inserting
the usual format/open# commands
in the BASIC but the dump is not
quite right (linefeeds?).

3. Why the SPRITE GENERATOR will
not work at all with microdrives
(it is supposed to). I think
ARTIST II is quite a lot better
than ART STUDIO but the handbook
(and backup?) is VERY inferior.

I joined PHANTOM BB but then
found I could not log on again.
VERY frustrating! I still need
help with my VOYAGER 7 modem and
NEWTERM comms software if there
is anyone out there who is fam-
iliar with them.

I have FLEXIPAGE 200. It is very
good indeed and could be very
useful in schools which still
have SPECTRUMS in use. Yes,it is
rather more difficult to operate
at first than its author seems

to think but he has been helpful
in sorting out problems and once
you get the hang of it, it
becomes quite straightforward
and quick to use (even for me).

Finally, congratulations on the
continuing quality of OUTLET. I
do hope circulation does expand
as it deserves. Programs like
ROTATOR, especially with the
later modification are excellent
and I also liked the banks of
character sets, although I
already had Sigmasoft's. A bank
of graphics/UDGs is what I am
looking for now.

               - CHRIS CLAYTON.

To Chris Clayton from Brian

I only have the 48K version of
Artist II.You don't say what the
problem is. If cassette handling
is from machine code it will be
very difficult to alter but if
it SAVEs and LOADs from BASIC as
the 48K version does then you
just alter the BASIC syntax. Use
OLIVER's READER from OUTLET 14
to read the headers of Artist II
on its own cassette then you
know the BASIC start line, code
lengths etc. It is difficult to
give more help without seeing
the software. Has anyone else
transferred this?

I too found myself unable to log
on to Phantom BB. I spent a lot

of money on long-distance phone
calls before giving up!

Why not try John Luby's FONT-GEN
in the Christmas issue. It makes
designing UDGs easy. You could
also raid OUTLET programs which
have had scores of them!

                         - Brian

From Mike Haine.

Dear Ron & Brian..

Reading Kelvin McWha's letter
prompts me to suggest he might
be put in touch with the Micro-
net 'Spectacular' lads who seem
well 'UP' on the +3. The contact
might be Brian Gaff.

This also prompts me to suggest
that OUTLET might provide a ser-
vice to help us to get in con-
tact with one another directly
either by phone, mbx. or letter.
John Nicholls' letter on Tas.2 &
Brian's reply reminds me that I
have been meaning to write on
that subject. I have found Tas 2
a very good prog. because not

only is it an adequate word
processer, but the fact that the
code routines are called from a
basic prog. makes it easier to
modify to suit one's own use. As
examples I have shortened the
BASIC without any loss in facil-
ities, so as to allow room for
quite a bit of extra code. The
routines I have added will carry
out various reformatting operat-
ions, such as to reformat 40
char/line Prestel mbx pages to
load directly into my terminal
sox, to reformat OUTLET text to
64 char/line for printing; to
print text prepared on tas2 in 2
64 char. columns, and a routine
to allow the preparation of
files (such as tel.nums.) to be
prepared easily (ideal for OU

index). There are many other
possibilities.It would be inter-
esting to know how many readers
of OUTLET have the prog. If a
goodly proportion it might be
developed as 'OUR SPECIAL'.
Comments on this and suggestions
for other improvements would be
of interest.... Brian how would
you propose to use interrupts to
get out of the write routine? I
have done quit a bit of search-
ing thro tas 2 code but have not
found it easy to locate relevant
routines. Like a lot of commerc-
ial code it is very badly organ-
ised.For example at what address
is the PC at this moment in
time?... I am much in favour of
the questionnaire idea. It would
be especially interesting to


have an analysis of the equipmnt
used by readers as well as the
main utility progs. available to
them and possibly their special
interests.
               Mike Haine.
I'm happy for OUTLET to be used
as a vehicle to make direct con-
tact with other Spectrum users,
Mike- in fact, it already HAS to
some extent.Anyone wishing their
address, telephone or mbx number
to be published in an OUTLETTER
must state this in each letter.

Re: using interrupts to exit the
Tasword 2 text editor,my routine
(called SAVESOON - next issue!)
does not check the position of
the PC but counts time and then
warns the user to SAVE the text!
                       - Brian

From: Peter Buchan


Dear R & B,

Many thanks for sending my first
issues of "OUTLET" complete with
the Sampler. I'm most impressed
with the whole thing-the quality
of the presentation, excellent
graphics, fantastically low cost
and range of subject matter.

 C * O * N * G * R * A * T * S

It would be interesting if you
could get your subscribers to
send in [details of] their
favourite utilities so that we
can all benefit from knowing
what's available.

I for one use:- Beta Basic, MDOC
and Trans Express. All three are
really professionally produced
and, in my opinion,indispensible
to anyone who likes hacking into
other's progs!!

Another idea!- You might like to
suggest to those who have their
letters or progs. published in
"OUTLET" that they include their
'phone numbers so that anyone
interested in doing so could get
in touch quickly.


Finally you might like to publ-
ish the following tips about the
Spectrum for those who get nasty
things happening from time to
time!

The Spectrum has a reputation
for unreliability. O.K. that's
true but "you gets what you pays
for" in this world and it is
after all a very cheap computer
for what it does.

Number one weak point -like many
electronic devices- CONNECTIONS!
The power plug/socket is top of
the list for faults. I have
changed the arrangement by
wiring a short (4 in.) length of
flex straight onto the board.
[the 9V plug NOT the mains power
plug! - BC]


This "tail" has a non-reversible
plug connected to it and a
matching socket comes up from

the power supply. I used a very
cheap speaker plug/socket
costing less than `1 and it's
been 100% reliable for a couple
of years.

(One could of course wire direct
to the power supply, but I've
found a reset straight from the
socket often gets rid of unex-
plainable happenings!!)


The ribbon cables between I/F 1
and the mdrives also cause
hassle. They are just not man
enough to stand bending about on
a regular basis. Answer?? Get a
length of chipboard about 12
inches long and five wide then
obtain a supply of double-sided

sticky tape. Clean up the multi-
way connectors thoroughly with
an ink rubber and polish with
your best white hankie. Make the
connections and then stick the
whole assembly to the board with
the tape. Result - reliability
like you've never had before.

New ribbon cables are available
from at least one supplier, and
it is wise to get a new one if
you've had problems with drives
"running away"from time to time.


So, hope that's of some use to
someone - don't forget to treat
the cartridges VERY carefully -
they seldom let one down if
treated properly I find.

If anyone wants a chat about
Spectrum problems give me a ring
on 0703-253532 (Peter Buchan is
the name) although my experience
is not THAT extensive!

All the best for Christmas Ron &
Brian and

     KEEP UP THE GOOD WORK!!

          Kind regards,

                  Peter.

Thanks,Peter! Happy New Year!
Regarding users' utilities - you
should enjoy Chris Clayton's
wide-ranging look at microdrive
software in CHECKOUT this month.
                   - Ron & Brian.

From John McCleave, Poole,Dorset

Dear Ron,

I am having trouble with one of
my Microdrives. It will accept
commands, i.e. CAT and the motor
will run...and run...and run,
without even the BREAK key dis-
abling it.The only way of stopp-
ing the motor is to reset the
computer and then enter 'STOP'.

I have tried all the simple
checks such as dirty/loose conn-
ections and, as I have a pair of
Microdrives, I think that Inter-
face 1 must be working correctly
as the other drive works O.K.

Are there any hardware checks

that I can make or have you any
idea what the problem could be?
I don't mind digging around
inside the drive. I would very
much appreciate any help that
you could give me,
                Best Regards,

                   John McCleave


To John McCleave from Brian

1. Disconnect the good drive and
re-test the bad one.

2. Re-check the ribbon cable(see
last letter from Peter Buchan)

3. Try Brian Gaff's DRIVECHAT 4.

4.While the casing's removed try
adjusting the speed(DRIVECHAT 14
(OPD test).You can run the drive
with casing removed if you hold
the cartridge with a finger.

5. Clean the record head with a
cassette head cleaner.

6  Ask MICROSAT on 0228 24579 if
they can repair it.

7.Boot it across the room and go
nid nid nid nnggaaaggggghhhhh!!!
(this may not work)

                       - Brian

From: Malcolm Goodman, Leeds



Dear Brian & Ron,

....can only say OUTLET is a joy
to use. Nicely put together and
VERY user-friendly especially
the options to COPY to printer.


On the minus side...

Oops!! #1 (OUTLET 15)
---------------------
In  the  48K  Spectrum  the  big
block of 255 (#FF) starts at
14446 (#0386E) and not #0385E as
stated in "Interlude",
[Quite right! - B.C.]

Oops!! #2 (OUTLET 15)
---------------------

In the same article you give an
example of how to set up a
vector table using the block
move instructions. Unfortunately
the error here is that the
source is shown as:

    LD HL,(64512)
    LD DE,(64513)
    etc.

Surely this should be

    LD HL,64512
    LD DE,64513
    etc.

[Quite right again! - B.C.]

Oops!! #3 (OUTLET 15)
---------------------
This one relates to OUTCLASS 4
and starts at Page 26 under Nib-
bles & Bytes.I feel that the way
it's described is very erroneous
and misleading. Surely it should
read that each bit starting at
the rightmost is 2 raised to the
power 0 then 1, 2...7 as we pro-
ceed to the leftmost bit?Further
more,the powers don't double as
we move leftwards-only the value
of that bit.The powers only move
up in steps of one.On the bottom
of Page 27 there is a numerical
example which further compounds
the error:
     (1!1)+(1!2)+(1!4)+(1!8)
    [!= upright arrow - B.C.]
    = 4 and NOT 15 as shown.

Also, this attempt to show
ascending powers does not relate
to the bit positions even if we
HAD got our sums right.
[3 NIL to you so far! - BC]

To anyone attempting to learn
about nibbles and bytes - my
sympathies!

Anyway, that's my two-pennyworth
said. It won't stop me enjoying
OUTLET each month[That's what
you think- all troublemakers
get suspended! - BC] as we
have so much to learn from each
other.

One query that I would raise
[Groan! - BC] though, Brian
is that I was always under the


impression that if exitting IM2
then RETI was used and not RET.
Am I correct in this thinking as
I've seen many people who only
use RET at the end of IM2?

     Best Regards,
         Malcolm Goodman

Strictly speaking I think that's
true but I've never been able to
find out why and what RETI does
that's different and why it's
not generally used. RET seems to
work alright so I've not pursued
it but I wonder? - Perhaps RETI
does an automatic EI or maybe it
is intended for use with add-on
hardware in IM1? I must admit to
knowing little about this. Does
anyone else know for sure?-Brian.
